title: Verb groups and the て-form
summary: Verbs come in three groups. Each group has its own recipe for the て-form and the た-form.

blocks.text: The **て-form** is the form a verb takes when something is attached to it. You already met it in lesson 4: **食べて**いる ("is eating") is the て-form 食べて plus いる. It is also how you link actions ("ate and went"), and later it lets you make requests and ask permission. The **た-form** is the plain past: **食べた** ("ate"). The two are made the same way, with **て** or **た** at the end.

To make the て-form or the た-form, first find out which of **three kinds** a verb is. Each kind has its own recipe. (Textbooks number these kinds differently from one another, so this course uses their names.)
An ichidan verb ends in **る**, and the kana just before る has an **い** or **え** sound. The recipe is easy: **drop る and add て or た**.
This is the biggest group. A godan verb can end in **any** う-row sound, and the て-form depends on that last kana.

blocks.title: How godan verbs make the て-form

blocks.text: So the past is 買った, 飲んだ, 歩いた, 泳いだ, 話した. One exception: **行く** becomes **行って** (past 行った), not 行いて. (死ぬ, to die, is the only verb that ends in ぬ.)
Some godan verbs also end in **いる** or **える**, so they look ichidan, but they follow the godan recipe: る becomes **って / った**. Learn these as you meet them.
A verb ending in **ある, うる or おる** (分かる, 作る, 取る) is **always godan**, so only verbs ending in いる or える can be confusing.
Only two, and you simply learn them.
You need the て-form for the ている form from lesson 4 ("is doing"). The white engine is the て-form, and いる is the real engine.
（私が）水を飲んでいる。 飲んで is the white engine.

blocks.title: Remember
items: **Ichidan** (い or え sound before る): drop **る**, add て / た.
**Godan**: look at the last kana (**う つ る → って**, **ぬ ぶ む → んで**, **く → いて**, **ぐ → いで**, **す → して**).
**行く → 行って / 行った** is the one godan exception.
Irregular: **来る → 来て / 来た**, **する → して / した**.
**ある・うる・おる** verbs are always godan; **帰る**, **走る** and **入る** are godan too.

questions.note: く becomes いて.

questions.instruction: What is the て-form of 読む?
questions.note: む becomes んで.

questions.instruction: What is the て-form of 待つ?
questions.note: つ becomes って.

questions.instruction: What is the past of 見る?
questions.note: Ichidan: drop る, add た.

questions.instruction: Which verb makes its て-form with んで?
questions.note: む becomes んで; く, つ and す do not.

questions.instruction: What is the て-form of 急ぐ?
questions.note: ぐ becomes いで.

questions.instruction: What is the て-form of 起きる?
questions.note: Ichidan: drop る, add て.

questions.instruction: What is the て-form of 帰る?
questions.note: 帰る is godan: る becomes って.

questions.instruction: What is the て-form of 行く?
questions.note: 行く is the one godan exception.

questions.instruction: What is the て-form of 来る?
questions.note: 来る is irregular: 来て (read きて).

questions.instruction: Which verb is ichidan?
questions.note: The others end in る but are godan.

questions.instruction: Which verb is godan?
questions.note: 入る looks ichidan but is godan.

questions.note: 待つ: つ becomes って.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap with the past of 遊ぶ
questions.note: 遊ぶ: ぶ becomes んだ in the past.

questions.instruction: True or false?
questions.prompt: 走る is an ichidan verb because it ends in る.
questions.note: 走る is godan: 走って.

questions.instruction: True or false?
questions.prompt: 昨日、本を読んだ。 The past 読んだ follows the む → んだ rule.
questions.note: む becomes んだ in the past: 読む → 読んだ.

questions.instruction: What is the て-form of する?
questions.note: する is irregular: して.
